events.title: Post-Election Listening, Healing & Sharing
events.description:
No matter the outcome of the election, there will inevitably be some chaos and confusion. There will be different stories swirling. There will be people talking at us all day.

This event will be an informal space to gather as a community to listen, heal & share in light of whatever is going on. This event will not be a space to hear the talking points that we will all be bombarded with by the news. Instead, we will take a break from those narratives, striking a different tone by dropping in together, sharing our voices, and feeling what emerges.

There will be light music, outdoor heaters & small circles of chairs for conversation. Blankets, pets and family members are welcome.

A note about COVID-19: Hand sanitizer will be provided. Masks are required, and we will be practicing social distancing for this event.

Location: This event will take place in the U St Neighborhood Association’s new Alley Park located between 12th and 13th Streets and between U and T Streets.

events.title: Sidewalk Palooza
events.description:
Every year DC launches a spring Potholepalooza event to rapidly identify and fix dangerous potholes. But while potholes get all the attention, our equally important sidewalks and pedestrian safety needs go neglected. The city's own data shows that the average pothole 311 request is fulfilled in 3 business days. Sidewalks are 270.

It's time to draw some attention to this discrepancy and the way that it makes life harder and less safe for everyone--especially people with disabilities, parents with strollers, and seniors. So let's come out together to document our neighborhoods' pedestrian infrastructure needs and build some community along the way.

We will meet at 4:00pm in Temperance Alley. We will do a stroll around the neighborhood to submit 311 requests and then we will do some chalk art together!

Please visit http://sidewalkpalooza.org/ for more info!

Hosted by Becca Kahn. Bring a poem or text or book that speaks to you, that's related to love and kindness. Or bring some thoughts you have had on what love and kindness mean (emotionally, spiritually, physically, ecologically, materially, socially) this week—maybe while you were boarding the bus, or sitting in your bedroom, or buying some broccoli at Trader Joe’s, or gazing at branches in the breeze, or calling your brother. You are all unfolding visionaries, associative speculators, gorgeous spirits, and illuminating thinkers—and we hope to host and nurture your exquisite minds!!! So bring a pen, some paper, perhaps a poem or text, and yourself. See ya there.

events.title: Native Land Acknowledgment Ceremony for Temperance Alley
events.description:
A Land Acknowledgement is a formal statement that recognizes and respects Native peoples as traditional stewards of lands. The statement highlights the enduring relationship between Native peoples and their traditional territories.

This Land Acknowledgement will be unique in that it recognizes two groups of previous inhabitants: the Indigenous and African-American peoples who lived in Temperance Alley and the surrounding area.

There will be some drumming from the African-American community present to open the ceremony. Armand Lione, the director of the DC Native History Project, will give a short presentation about the significance of the land to the Native Anacostan Indians when they lived here.

Regarding the importance of land acknowledgement events, Chelsea Vowel, a Métis woman from the Plains Cree speaking community of Lac Ste. Anne, Alberta, writes:

“If we think of territorial acknowledgments as sites of potential disruption, they can be transformative acts that to some extent undo Indigenous erasure. I believe this is true as long as these acknowledgments discomfit both those speaking and hearing the words. The fact of Indigenous presence should force non-Indigenous peoples to confront their own place on these lands.”

A sign with the written land acknowledgment will be installed in Temperance Alley. The sign will read:

We recognize that this land was once the land of the Anacostan peoples. We acknowledge the Anacostan people, and the people of the greater Piscataway Indian Nation, as the first custodians of this land.

We recognize the residents who lived in Temperance Alley during the 1800s and 1900s. Square 274, as it was referred to in official city documents, had 62 adults and 72 children living in 26 dwellings in 1953. A sociologist in 1953 who spent time here stated that, "there is camaraderie among old tenants." We celebrate that camaraderie, and we hope to sustain it.

As neighbors, we pay our respects to all Indigenous, Black, and other groups of people -- past, present and future -- who have relationships to this place. We honor their connection to this land. This history is not a relic of the past. It is a part of our unfolding relationship to this place. We acknowledge this history with an eye to the generations to follow us.

The event begins at 7:30pm. We will have candles in the garden to foster an environment conducive for our exploration together. You are encouraged to bring something related to forgiveness and grace: a totem that means something to you, a poem or excerpt from a reading, or a story from your life. Writing materials will be provided, but you are encouraged to bring your own.

Our agenda for the evening is as follows:

• Gather in the garden and land together with a grounding exercise
• Read excerpts on forgiveness and grace
• Individually reflect and journal
• Group exploration and discussion

We welcome everyone. We see you — you unfolding visionaries, you associative speculators, you gorgeous spirits, you illuminating thinkers. We honor you, and we ask for your grace in attending this event.

events.title: Mystical Tales: A Writing Workshop
events.description:
Fantasy, horror, magical realism, folklore, and mythology...

In this writing workshop, let's cast spells with our words to change what we fear, resent, and ignore in our lives and in our worlds. We'll provide writing materials, though you are encouraged to bring your own if you'd like. This workshop includes time at the end to share your writing with others if you would like to.

Please wear warm clothing. We will have blankets to lie on and candles spread throughout the garden for lighting in addition the streetlights in the alley.

We will cap the group at 15 participants total to foster an intimate, immersive group environment. Please register on Eventbrite to make sure you have a spot!

About the host: This workshop is led by Amanda Liaw. Amanda (she/they) is a Media & Communications Associate for the PEN/Faulkner Foundation where she advocates passionately for the power of literary education in shaping lives and communities. Growing up in Singapore with a love for all forms of storytelling, she views her prior experiences in film production, stage management, and digital media strategy through an interdisciplinary lens, with narrative at the heart of human connection and empathetic understanding as its purpose.

events.title: Ecstatic Dance in the Garden
events.description:
Neighbors dancing their booties off at our first silent disco event in August

Ecstatic Dance DC is back! And they are partnering with us at Temperance Alley Garden to host an ecstatic dance this Thursday evening from 7pm - 9pm. There will be another Ecstatic Dance on Friday morning from 7:00am - 9:30am. Tickets are $20 for the individual Evening and Morning events or $30 for both. Please register and purchase your tickets on Eventbrite at this link.

Costumes highly encouraged. It’s Halloween week - so wear something silly, provocative or fun. Have a funky onesie you' haven’t worn in forever? Throw that baby on!

What is Ecstatic Dance? Ecstatic Dance is a community gathering for people who want to express themselves in a playful and artistic space with other people who value conscious connection, movement, and music.

Ecstatic Dance is the “dance-iest dance floor in all of DC.” There will be a diversity of expressions and generations show up for one thing: to dance. All magic and connection sprouts from that singular intention. Our barefoot, non-verbal, lucid space is curated for you to let loose, play, commune with your body and connect with others in a vibrant setting. This event will be a Silent Disco Ecstatic Dance. Headphones will be provided.

Soundtrack and DJ: Ursidae Music

COVID Safety Protocols: With regard to public health and our commitment to making Ecstatic Dance as safe as possible, we will be requiring either proof of vaccination OR a negative covid test within 72 hours before the dance begins. Thank you for your help keeping our community safe!

———————

First time to an Ecstatic Dance? Here's an introduction to what we're about:

Ecstatic Dance is a community gathering for people who want to express themselves in a playful and artistic space with other people who value conscious connection, movement, and great music!

We create a dance/movement space that is inspiring and uplifting, without talking, alcohol or nightclub vibes. We encourage participants to utilize the Ecstatic Dance space as a laboratory for creative movement, unbridled self-expression, authentic connections and a healthy dose of sweat.

We hold a nonverbal, barefoot, alcohol-free container to keep the journey intentional and lucid.

***

Guidelines:

1. No talking on the dance floor

2. Drug-Free, Smoke-Free, Alcohol-Free environment

3. No photos or videos, cellphones muted and out of sight

4. Respect for the space and for one another

5. Move your body however you wish!

6. You can dance alone, or with partners. (If you’d rather not dance with someone, thank them for the offer by placing your hands in prayer position at your heart)

***

What to Bring:

1. Loose-fitting clothes that let you move your body and free yourself

2. Water and a water bottle. You can refill it at the venue.

First time to an Ecstatic Dance? Here's an introduction to what we're about:

Ecstatic Dance is a community gathering for people who want to express themselves in a playful and artistic space with other people who value conscious connection, movement, and great music!

We create a dance/movement space that is inspiring and uplifting, without talking, alcohol or nightclub vibes. We encourage participants to utilize the Ecstatic Dance space as a laboratory for creative movement, unbridled self-expression, authentic connections and a healthy dose of sweat.

We hold a nonverbal, barefoot, alcohol-free container to keep the journey intentional and lucid.

***

Guidelines:

1. No talking on the dance floor

2. Drug-Free, Smoke-Free, Alcohol-Free environment

3. No photos or videos, cellphones muted and out of sight

4. Respect for the space and for one another

5. Move your body however you wish!

6. You can dance alone, or with partners. (If you’d rather not dance with someone, thank them for the offer by placing your hands in prayer position at your heart)

***

What to Bring:

1. Loose-fitting clothes that let you move your body and free yourself

2. Water and a water bottle. You can refill it at the venue.

events.title: Qigong with Nicole Jackson
events.description:
Qigong is an ancient energy cultivation practice that literally translates into “energy work”. In Qigong, we utilize the power of our breath, postures, movement, and meditation to clear, align, circulate, and strengthen our Qi. Qi means vital life-force energy. There are so many health benefits of practicing Qigong. Not just on a physical level, but also emotionally, mentally, and spiritually. According to the Taoist philosophy, all dis-ease originates from blocked or stagnant energy flow. Therefore, it is believed that every condition can be improved with better energy flow, thus the practice of Qigong. The question then becomes, "Why not practice Qigong?" ​

Here are 10 proven benefits of regularly practicing Qigong:
* Relieves Chronic Muscle Pain
* Relieves Anxiety & Depression
* Improves Cognitive Function
* Lowers Blood Pressure
* Improves Sleep
* Boosts Energy Levels
* Increases Bone Density
* Boosts Immune System
* Relieves Mental & Emotional Stress
* Relieves Arthritis Pain

In this class participants will learn how to tune into their internal life-force, clear stagnant energy from the body’s organs and meridians, as well as strengthen and harmonize their Qi through various Qigong exercises. All levels are welcome.

events.title: “When the Earth Started to Sing” a sonic journey
events.description:
We’ll gather in the garden at sunset to listen to David Haskell’s original piece from Emergence Magazine together.

“This sonic journey written and narrated by David G. Haskell brings us to the beginning of sound and song on planet Earth. The experience is made entirely of tiny trembling waves in air, the fugitive, ephemeral energy that we call sound. Spoken words combined with terrestrial sounds invite our senses and imaginations to go outward into an experience of the living Earth and its history. How did the vast and varied chorus of modern sounds—from forest to oceans to human music—emerge from life’s community? When did the living Earth first start to sing? We invite you on a journey into deep time and deep sound that will open your ears and your imagination.”

events.title: Qigong Series with Nicole Jackson
events.description:
Week 2 Six Healing Sounds Qigong

The Healing Sounds is a powerful and transformative practice that helps to clear toxic emotions from our field. As we do this, we work to heal and balance our organ systems and liberate stagnant energy that keeps us vibrating on lower levels. The healing sounds provide clearing and recalibrating of our energy and allow space to embrace more positive emotional fields within our bodies and our lives.

This 6-week series is hosted by instructor Nicole Jackson of Healthy Soul Wellness. All levels are welcome. We can’t guarantee you’ll be a pro but you will definitely have a better sense of Qi, feel better in your body, be clearer in your mind, become more energetically aligned, and have learned a few Qigong forms in the process.

events.title: Autumnal Equinox Celebration 🌞
events.description:
Join neighbors in the garden at dusk to ring in the Fall, reflect on the Summer, and share in harvest snacks.

Since the Summer Solstice back in June our nights have been growing longer and our days have been shortening. On September 22nd we’ll celebrate the Autumnal Equinox (equal-night) when the sun passes most directly over the equator and the day and night are of equal length. This marks the mid-point in our seasonal journey towards the Winter Solstice in December.

This family-friendly gathering is hosted by the Garden Stewards

events.description:
Week 4 Tai Chi Qigong (Shibashi)

Shibashi means Eighteen Movements. This is a popular Qigong Flow form that consists of 18 movements. Qigong Flow is characterized by repetitive movements that flow from one to the next.

From my own study of this form, I feel that it really focuses on creating balance in the body by covering all eight actions of Qi Flow. The gentle rocking movements left and right and back and forth stretch the meridians, improve circulation and digestion.

This free 6-week series is hosted by instructor Nicole Jackson of Healthy Soul Wellness. All levels are welcome. events.title: 🎂 Temperance Alley Garden's 2nd Birthday Party 🎈🎈🎈
events.description:
Happy 2nd Birthday to the Temperance Alley Garden!

Hard to believe it's already been two years since we first unlocked the gates and cut down the barbed wire. A lot has happened in a relatively short amount of time. Our volunteers have now hosted over 250 events of different shapes and sizes, which have brought healing, entertainment, education, and conviviality to the neighborhood. Our programming has included workshops on ecology, writing, photography, painting, mushroom cultivation, and oral history; wellness classes like Qigong, Yoga, and group meditation; cultural events like Music in the Garden, charity art markets, neighborhood picnics, and holiday celebrations. We’re also well on our way towards growing 1,500 lbs of produce this season, including squash, watermelon, beans, pepper, tomato, kale, bok choy, collard greens, and more.

Join the U Street Neighborhood Association for a celebration of the garden and all the wonderful hosts, volunteers, and participants who bring the space to life.

It's also great to support healthy hormones, sexual energy, fertility, and longevity. Since this is long-term immune support, this routine should be used consistently over time and can be used all year round.

events.title: U Street Neighborhood Association Quarterly Meeting
events.location: Thurgood Marshall Center, 1816 12th Street Northwest, Washington, DC 20009
events.description:
On Wednesday 4/19 we'll be holding our first quarterly membership meeting of 2023, from 6–7:30pm at the Thurgood Marshall Center (1816 12th St NW).

Completed in 1912, this building was once home to the 12th Street YMCA—one of the most important 20th century institutions of the U Street neighborhood. Teddy Roosevelt helped lay the cornerstone at the groundbreaking ceremony for the Y, which served as a meeting space for countless community organizations. Read all about it before seeing it in person: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twelfth_Street_YMCA_Building

At our meeting we'll...

• Hear what's new with USNA's committees on Harrison Park, Temperance Alley, and public safety
• Discuss the 1250 U Street planned unit development and our goals for 2023
• Host a book swap to jumpstart the USNA lending library

I'm excited our association is becoming a network for hyperlocal learning. To keep the educational energy ablaze, bring 1 or 2 books you'd like to share with a neighbor—and you'll leave with a new rabbit hole to explore. After the meeting, we'll head over to Open Piano Night & drinks at The Saloon on U Street.

Spring is the best time to pot up plants — the warming weather coinciding with fresh soil for the roots leads to a pleasant growing season even for our indoor babies. There are many reasons to repot and pot up plants, including providing the roots with more space & increasing the nutrients available in the soil. events.title: "Seed to Soul" Connecting Communities of Color back to Nature through Urban Gardening
events.description:
Soul Trak is a DC based non-profit whose mission is to diversify the outdoors by connecting communities of color to outdoor spaces and activities while developing future environmental and community stewards and leaders. Soul Trak's 2023 Environmental Leaders Cohort, made up of 12 emerging outdoor leaders from around the DMV, are excited to present their community initiative, "Seed to Soul", an engaging day of exploring a local urban garden space. The mission of our program is to reconnect communities of color to nature, and to strengthen relationships to nature through the exploration of our food environment. By highlighting gardening as an easy accessible way to connect with nature, the cohort hopes to foster empowerment to Black and Brown families to redefine their relationship with the outdoors.

The Seed to Soul Initiative will host a gardening education workshop and discussion on how to take care of our environment. We will be providing mini grow kits and have interactive activities for all ages to participants.

coon is an experimental exploration of black femininity and ritual. Set in the middle of the woods, a gang of raccoons create a community of love with the pressure of raccoon hunters. How do these rituals of love create a space of serenity and peace?

events.title: 2 QuTe 4 COViD Safety: an outdoor Masked Mixer
events.description:
This event will center Two Spirit, queer, trans, and intersex folks that hold interest in raising COVID-consciousness within 2SQTI+ community and give community care to all of us experiencing impacts of rolling viral resurgences.

Notable logistics: booze free; attendance requests on honor system (for 10-14 days leading up to event, practice of masking on public transit, grocery store, hospital spaces, plus avoiding high risk spaces with large crowds when possible); pre-event testing request on honor system (nose, cheek + throat swab), potluck style food sharing with tupperware to facilitate consumption off-site, and specific mask types (N95 or KN95).

This is a co-production by a network of covid-conscious community groups in the DC metro area, DC Trans Picnics, @2quties, and @lookoutlia, among others.

Open to all, please let us know if you have any accessibility questions or concerns.

events.title: DC Sing-Along Night
events.description:
The D.C. Sing-Along is a hootenanny for the digital age. Combining the communal spirit of '60s sing-alongs with a modern songbook and rawk 'tude, the D.C. Sing-Along is a heartwarming, cathartic, and analog good time.

How It Works:

• Bring an acoustic instrument: Anyone's welcome to join the “band,” from fretters to flautists of all skill levels! The D.C. Sing-Along Songbook includes chords for the musicians.
• Or just bring your voice: Musical ability is NOT required. Nobody will be able to hear you sing, so don’t feel self-conscious!
• Call out your fave song from the songbook: The Beatles, Disney, Lizzo, Whitney — the D.C. Sing-Along Songbook has something for everyone!
• Bring the kids, too: As long as you're ok with a smidge of profanity (looking at you, Alanis).

Questions? Email dcsingalong@gmail.com

events.title: Snailmail Station × Offline Night 🧱 a Sunday Playtest
events.location: 1909 13th Street Northwest, Washington, DC 20009
events.description:
In our age of hyperconnectivity and non-stop texting, it can be hard to find the time to send a longform letter through the good ole snail mail. There’s probably someone you’ve been meaning to reach out to, someone you’ve always wanted to be pen pals with, someone who would appreciate holding your message in their hands. Snailmail Station is about setting aside the time to practice the art of correspondence, together. We’ll have hot apple cider, baked goods, water color materials, writing materials + stamps on-hand and send you off to the local mailbox. Bring a can-do attitude, addresses of a few old friends (or do that later), artistic inspiration, and some fall layers -- the forecast says 61 and sunny, but will get chilly as the sun sets.
Hosted by Aaron, Danny, & Tali

events.title: Refugee Stories & Film Screening with the IRC
events.description:
Through this event, the International Rescue Committee seeks to engage members of the community in the Northwest Washington, D.C. area and beyond, with stories told by refugees uprooted by war and conflict.

We’ll be screening the film “This is Home” which follows four Syrian families as they move through the IRC Support system. The challenges faced by refugees – both during migratory events, and through the resettlement process – are difficult, and highly unique. They are also highly relevant in global society.

Participants will also learn more about Temperance Garden and neighborhood history, including Civil War refugee stories from the former site of Camp Barker down the street (now Garrison Elementary).

hosted by Michael and the IRC

events.description:
Step inside the Temperance Garden time machine and learn about the relationship between urban planning, public health, and architecture through the story of alley life in Washington D.C. Our city was once home to hundreds of inhabited alleyways, “parallel worlds” where the city’s poorest residents built their livelihoods and communities of care. What was life like in the often-forgotten spaces between the streets? What became of these alley communities and why? How might these untold histories shape the future of urban design in our neighborhoods? We’ll explore these questions and more in conversation with Carolyn Swope, a doctoral student in urban planning at Columbia University, and Kim Williams, an architectural historian with the Office of Planning and author of the newly published book Hidden Alleyways of Washington D.C.

Carolyn Swope is a doctoral student in urban planning at Columbia University, and also holds a Master of Public Health. Broadly, her research interests focus on the relationship between housing and health disparities. She recently published an article examining the weaponization of health disparities by reformers pushing for alley clearance.

Kim Williams is an architectural historian with a particular interest in researching local history, neighborhoods, and urban planning developments in and around Washington, D.C. For the past 15 years, she’s been working in the D.C. Historic Preservation Office, where she am engaged in the research and historical designation of buildings, neighborhoods, and institutional districts.

Hosted by Aaron

• Call out your fave song from the songbook: The Beatles, Disney, Lizzo, Whitney — the D.C. Sing-Along Songbook has something for everyone!
• Bring the kids, too: As long as you're ok with a smidge of profanity (looking at you, Alanis).

Questions? Email dcsingalong@gmail.com

events.title: New Moon Picnic & Ritual 🌑
events.description:
Gather with us for a New Moon picnic and embrace the energy of the new moon!

Enjoy a magical evening filled with connection, nourishment, and spiritual exploration. Bring your own snacks, set out a blanket on the grass, and set intentions for the June lunar cycle with a simple ritual.

Plus, dive into a celestial exploration of yourself with astrology readings and a selection of specially brewed herbal teas ✨

Hosted by Skye and LJ

events.description: Come make and share zines in the garden with DC Zinefest! Materials provided, free and open to the public. Check us out on Instagram @DCZinefest or email dczinefest@gmail.com for more information.

events.title: Garden Volunteer Hours
events.description:
Come get your hands in the soil with our partners at Farm the District, every Saturday throughout the growing season. Whether you’re a first-timer or returning veteran, all are needed to help tend to our shared backyard.

There’s plenty of projects to keep all hands busy, including weeding, watering, composting, repairing, crafting, and ongoing side projects. Find a partner and choose your own adventure. And don’t forget to take home your share of the communal harvest.

As always, we’ll also be giving an orientation tour for newcomers. Welcome neighbors!

events.title: SharingCircle: the Speed of Life

The community grows the garden and the garden grows the community.

Join us to cultivate community and connect in this first of its kind offering. All are welcome, introverts and social butterflies alike. We hope to create a judgment free space where folks participate in a way that feels best to them! First topic we’ll explore: The Speed of Life.

Hosted by Rachel and Nathalia

events.title: Juneteenth Celebration at Harrison Park
events.location: Harrison Recreation Center, 1330 V Street Northwest, Washington, DC 20009
events.description:
Join your neighbors at the Harrison Rec Center as we come together to host an afternoon of activities for our second annual Juneteenth Celebration!

This is a youth-centered community event that will feature face painting, art making, and live music. Plus a basketball tournament on the newly remodeled court.

The U Street Neighborhood Association has spent the past few years getting the space back open, and this event will also serve as a community celebration alongside the newly renovated V Street Studio. Various membership-based community organizing groups focusing on black liberation, economic empowerment, health equity, and access to early learning in DC, as well as other national organizations, will join this year's effort.

Event activities include:

• Live Band
• Face Painting
• Basketball Giveaway
• Basketball Tournament
• Community Speakers
• Coloring Mural
• V Street Studio Gallery Tour

In partnership with our friends at Long Live GoGo, U Street Main Street, DPR, and the Kiwanis Club — this artistic activation is designed to uplift platforms from various backgrounds throughout the DMV, engage inner-city youth, and unite the culture of the metropolitan area. We hope to see you there!

events.description:
Summer is officially here as the sun reaches it’s northernmost point in our sky. On the longest day of the year we’ll gather in the Garden for a sunset potluck and grillout.

Activities include a celestial time-keeping demonstration, letter writing reflection, and solstice art creation (with mulberry paint!). Plus an open mic will be stationed on the lawn for any and all aspiring poets, musicians, and spoken word performers.

Folks are encouraged (but not required) to bring food and drink to share — especially mulberries!! — as well as any Solstice rituals that they’d like to lead.

events.description:
Amazing live comedy made up on the spot! 🎉 This time, it's all about you! Dive into our splash-zone themed all-play jam. No performances, no instruction, just pure improv magic.

events.description:

This family-friendly event is designed for ages 3-12 & snacks will be provided.

events.title: Meditation Jam for Musicians 🎶
events.description:
Stop overthinking and let the music flow.

We often force ourselves to play what we think will sound good, but sometimes the best music happens when stop pushing ourselves. In this experimental jam, we’ll try to get out of our own way and let the music flow without judgement.

Open to musicians of all skill levels.

Hosted by Russell

events.title: TAG HouseKeeping Circle
events.description:
Our official calendaring meeting for the month of July. Bring any business you may have or partner with at Stump Fellow to program your submitted event ideas.

Anyone can join as we discuss garden event planning, budgeting, and partnerships. Your ideas and energy are more than welcome!

*HouseKeeping Circles happen at the end of each month, they are the functional meetings where we calendar events for the next month of programming, approve any new spending, and can vote to change any Garden policies if needed. These meetings have official minutes that keep a record of our decisions and are shared with the rest of the U Street Neighborhood Association for transparency.

events.title: Embodying The Elements: Exploring Nature with Movement
events.description:
Join Sisi SoulShine of Soul Shine Theater Garden at Temperance Alley for a playful dance workshop to move your body and connect with the nature that surrounds us.

Through dance and movement, we will listen to ourselves, actively reflect on our relationship to nature, and embody various natural elements: roots, water, fire, trees etc…

You will be guided by Sisi SoulShine while also having the space to generate your own unique movements through practices of self consent, boundaries, and improvisation. You do not need any previous dance experience, only the desire to explore, learn, dance, and the commitment to connect to your body. While in shared space, we will celebrate each other and embody play and joy as ways of collective liberation.

An optional RSVP to our free workshop is here. Please consider supporting Soul Shine Theater Garden with a donation at the gate.

events.title: Sunday Yoga with Movement for Choice
events.description:
🌺 Joy is My Justice ~ Grounding Yoga Flow 🌺

Join Movement for Choice for a grounding evening yoga flow for NVRDC at Temperance Alley Garden on Sunday, August 25th at 5pm. We will be exploring the expansion and contraction of joy in our bodies and with the earth, including practices of vocal toning and self-inquiry. Hope you join us!!

Temperance Alley Garden offers community donation-suggested classes with the beautiful greenery and open blue sky. Perfect for grounding and centering. Bring yourself, water, and a mat.

Network for Victim Recovery DC (NVRDC) is a nonprofit empowering victims of all crimes to achieve survivor-defined justice through free advocacy, case management, and legal services in DC. 100% of all proceeds from this class go directly toward their cause.

Movement for Choice is a DC-based nonprofit fighting for reproductive justice through donation-based movement classes and events.

events.title: Music in the Garden!
events.description:
Featuring David Stevenson + Swataa & Tiff

Join the Garden plants and critters for an evening of home-grown music! Somewhere between a house show and barnyard jam. While tipping is encouraged, the event is free and open to all. Bring a blanket to sit on and snacks to share :)

David Stevenson @dsteve_dc is a local singer-songwriter in Northwest DC. He brings a high-energy guitar style to his solo and full-band shows, local festivals, and songwriter events all over the DMV. David’s most recent EP “Next Time” is out now on all streaming services.

Swataa (@Swataa) has been releasing independently produced songs since 2020, and is inspired by nature and connecting to our emotions through songwriting. Her latest single “Infatuated Dreaming” is out now, which is part of a larger unreleased project. You can hear them play with a full band (w/Tiff) at their headline show on 9/19 at the Pocket in DC!

Tiff (@twimenta.music) is a queer singer-songwriter living in Northwest DC. She is inspired to share her heartaches, joys, and curiosities in hopes that they resonate with her listeners. Tiff is new to sharing their music with the wider world, so keep an eye out for them on Instagram or at the local open mics! She is excited to connect with other musicians, so if you want to collab, make sure to say hello!

Swataa & Tiff met right here at Temperence Alley Garden during a Thursday community jam sesh! They quickly hit it off with their love for lyricism and processing life’s experiences through music.

produced by Stephen

Discover the power of empathetic communication in this introduction to Nonviolent Communication (NVC). events.title: Snailmail Station
events.description:
In our age of hyperconnectivity and non-stop texting, it can be hard to find the time to send a longform letter through the good ole snail mail. There’s probably someone you’ve been meaning to reach out to, someone you’ve always wanted to be pen pals with, someone who would appreciate holding your message in their hands. Snailmail Station is about setting aside the time to practice the art of correspondence, together.

We’ll have writing materials + stamps on-hand and send you off to the local mailbox. Bring a can-do attitude, addresses of a few old friends (or do that later), and artistic inspiration.

events.title: Autumnal Equinox Celebration 🌞 Pawpaw Paw-tluck
events.description:
Join neighbors at dusk to ring in the Fall, reflect on the Summer, and celebrate pawpaw season!

Since the Summer Solstice back in June our nights have been growing longer and our days have been shortening. We’ll celebrate the Autumnal Equinox (equal-night) when the sun passes most directly over the equator and the day and night are of equal length. This marks the mid-point in our seasonal journey towards the Winter Solstice in December.

We’ll also be celebrating the beloved Pawpaw – the only tropical fruit native to the DMV! Prepare your favorite pawpaw dish/recipe and come ready to sample others. If you need help acquiring pawpaws reach out in the TAG WhatsApp group.

This family-friendly gathering is hosted by the Garden Stewards.

events.title: Music in the Garden! ft. Rachel Ellis & Mar Rose
events.description:
Rachel Ellis (@curlycutieray) is new to singer-songwriting. For the past year, in her cozy apartment in Alexandria, she’s delved into the world of storytelling through music. Her current project, yet to be released, is one that expresses themes of love, loss, and self actualization during bouts of transition and change through ethereal, confessional lyricism. She’s excited to be playing all of her originals for a live audience for the first time at Temperance Alley Garden!

Mar Rose (@marbloomingrose) is a singer/songwriter born and raised in the DMV. Mar began songwriting in their early years. They were encouraged by their musical family to learn guitar in order to accompany their original vocal melodies. Influenced by classic rock, folk rock, grunge, reggae, and punk, Mar established in their middle and high school years a diverse repertoire, and a sound of their own was beginning to emerge. By the end of college, Mar had experience performing in multiple bands, duets, a cappella ensembles, and as a solo artist. Mar continues to perform throughout the DC and Baltimore region.

Mar has released music under "Mar Rose", their solo act, as well as with their former band, "The Feelz," and under, "Blooming Rose," an experimental self-produced project. Mar released their first studio album in 2022, titled, "Humble Heart" and is currently working on a new record.

events.title: Queer Black Broadway Walking Tour
events.location: Begins at Howard Theater; ends at Thurst Lounge, 2204 14th Street, Washington, DC
events.description:
In this very special tour to celebrate LGBTQ History Month, Off the Mall Tours is partnering with the Rainbow History Project to bring you the Queer Black Broadway walking tour. The U Street Corridor was known as "Black Broadway" in its heyday of the early 20th Century. From the Prohibition Era to the Civil Rights Movement, it was also the center for social justice and fringe movements that fought to bring more opportunity for marginalized groups, including a secretive but active Queer community that was associated with the Harlem Renaissance, the Pansy Craze, underground crime worlds, and the wide world of entertainment. This 1.5 hour walking tour begins at Howard Theater and ends at Thurst Lounge, 2204 14th Street, which is DC's only queer black-owned bar! A portion of proceeds go to benefit the Rainbow History Project.

The Rainbow History Project’s mission is to collect, preserve, and promote an active knowledge of the history, arts, and culture of metropolitan Washington DC’s diverse LGBTQ+ communities.

Silence Echoez is a singer/songwriter from the DC are whose tunes come in flavors from café ambience to protest anthem. As the drummer for bands such as ilyAIMY and Emma G, he approaches songwriting with a nuanced sense of rhythm that often incorporates the influences of these original groups as well.

No Cheese is a Pop Power Pop trio with roots in Southeastern PA. The group is composed of Matthew Gargano on vocals and lead guitar, Sara Mack on vocals and bass guitar, and Connor Gephart on drums. events.title: Queer Black Broadway Walking Tour
events.location: 620 T Street Northwest, Washington, DC 20001 (starting point: Howard Theater; tour concludes at Thurst Lounge, 2204 14th Street)
events.description:
This Martin Luther King Jr. weekend, Off the Mall Tours is partnering with the Rainbow History Project to bring you the Queer Black Broadway walking tour. The U Street Corridor was known as "Black Broadway" in its heyday of the early 20th Century. From the Prohibition Era to the Civil Rights Movement, it was also the center for social justice and fringe movements that fought to bring more opportunity for marginalized groups, including a secretive but active Queer community that was associated with the Harlem Renaissance, the Pansy Craze, and the Civil Rights Movement, including the planner of the March for Jobs and Freedom Bayard Rustin, a gay black man. This 1.5 hour walking tour begins at Howard Theater and ends at Thurst Lounge, 2204 14th Street, which is DC's only queer black-owned bar! A portion of proceeds go to benefit the Rainbow History Project.

The Rainbow History Project’s mission is to collect, preserve, and promote an active knowledge of the history, arts, and culture of metropolitan Washington DC’s diverse LGBTQ+ communities. You can find more information about them at https://www.rainbowhistory.org/.

The D.C. Sing-Along is a hootenanny for the digital age. Combining the communal spirit of '60s sing-alongs with a modern songbook and rawk 'tude, the D.C. Sing-Along is a heartwarming, cathartic, and analog good time.

How It Works:

• Bring an acoustic instrument: Anyone's welcome to join the “band,” from fretters to flautists of all skill levels! The D.C. Sing-Along Songbook includes chords for the musicians.
• Or just bring your voice: Musical ability is NOT required. Nobody will be able to hear you sing, so don’t feel self-conscious!
• Call out your fave song from the songbook: The Beatles, Disney, Lizzo, Whitney — the D.C. Sing-Along Songbook has something for everyone!
• Bring the kids, too: As long as you're ok with a smidge of profanity (looking at you, Alanis).

Questions? Email dcsingalong@gmail.com

events.title: The History of Our Neighborhood, Revealed Through Architecture
events.location: Thurgood Marshall Center, 1816 12th Street Northwest, Washington, DC 20009
events.description:
The DC Preservation League was founded as Don't Tear It Down in 1971 when the Old Post Office building on Pennsylvania Avenue, NW, was slated to be demolished. Community members came together to save it and soon other buildings across the District were being preserved. The DC Preservation League was established with the mission to preserve, protect, and enhance the historic and built environment of Washington, DC. Their work continues today through many initiatives— for example, check out their newly launched efforts to track buildings designed by African American architects.

We’ll hear from Zachary Burt, Community Outreach and Grants Manager for the DC Preservation League, He is the staff liaison for the Landmarks Committee and the Government Affairs Committee, and works with the Historic Districts Coalition. In addition to his work on historic landmark nominations, Zach manages DCPL’s Preservation Initiatives Grant Program and the DC Historic Sites website and cellular phone app. He holds a B.S. in Political Science from the University of Utah and an M.A. in Historic Preservation from Goucher College. Zach is passionate about DC’s rich history, culture, and architecture, and loves exploring the city’s many neighborhoods.

Everyone is welcome! Please RSVP here to join us.

Featuring local singer-songwriters Pat Smith and Shaman Jones. Our pre-show OPEN MIC will run from 6-7pm for any musicians, poets, & artists who’d like to share their talents!

Born and raised in Cheverly, MD. Pat was introduced to music at an early age. At 19, Pat made a life-altering decision to enlist in the U.S. Navy, choosing to serve aboard a Ballistic submarine. His time in the Navy profoundly shaped his perspective, both as an individual and as an artist. The solitude and isolation of submarine life became a fertile ground for songwriting. Pat will be releasing his first album entitled "Functioning?" this summer, with singles from the album already available on streaming platforms.

Shaman Jones is a singer-songwriter from Cheverly, MD. His music is a piano-based mix of classical, rock, folk, and RnB, which can be likened to the works of Tori Amos, Ben Folds, and Fiona Apple. Shaman seeks to create lyrical narratives which are equal parts confessional and contemplative. His most recent project, “Variations on a One-Night Stand”, is a collection of modern folk songs which explore the complex emotional landscapes of different types of relationships.

Join the Garden plants and critters for an evening of home-grown music –– somewhere between a house show and barnyard jam. While tipping the artists is encouraged, the event is free and open to all. Bring a blanket to sit on and snacks to share :)

events.description:
To be in relationship with land is to know who lives there...

We will walk through the “Temperance Sanctuary” (the parcel across from TAG) and say hello by identifying the plant neighbors in the plot. After identifying and inventorying the plant neighbors, we will draw plant portraits to create an initial blueprint of the Temperance Sanctuary.

The Temperance Sanctuary is a new extension of the Temperance Alley Garden – a place to quiet down, to observe, and to cultivate reciprocity between ourselves and the land. Come join us in the visioning and stewardship of Temperance Sanctuary: as a time capsule of Indigenous history and stewardship, native food/micro forest to bring back native biodiversity, and an ecological classroom to foster and practice our stewardship. If you’re interested in any of these topics, we welcome you to join us in its design and execution!

events.title: Music in the Garden
events.description:
Rescheduled from 5/30: Featuring local singer-songwriters Pat Smith and Shaman Jones.

Born and raised in Cheverly, MD. Pat was introduced to music at an early age. At 19, Pat made a life-altering decision to enlist in the U.S. Navy, choosing to serve aboard a Ballistic submarine. His time in the Navy profoundly shaped his perspective, both as an individual and as an artist. The solitude and isolation of submarine life became a fertile ground for songwriting. Pat will be releasing his first album entitled "Functioning?" this summer, with singles from the album already available on streaming platforms.

Shaman Jones is a singer-songwriter from Cheverly, MD. His music is a piano-based mix of classical, rock, folk, and RnB, which can be likened to the works of Tori Amos, Ben Folds, and Fiona Apple. Shaman seeks to create lyrical narratives which are equal parts confessional and contemplative. His most recent project, “Variations on a One-Night Stand”, is a collection of modern folk songs which explore the complex emotional landscapes of different types of relationships.

Join the Garden plants and critters for an evening of home-grown music –– somewhere between a house show and barnyard jam. While tipping the artists is encouraged, the event is free and open to all. Bring a blanket to sit on and snacks to share :)

In this session, we’ll spend time tending to the Temperance Sanctuary through acts of gentle stewardship—clearing debris, picking up trash, and making space for new life to emerge. Through group discussion and shared observation, we’ll begin imagining the future of this space—what kinds of native plants, beings, and relationships do we want to nurture?

The Temperance Sanctuary is a new extension of the Temperance Alley Garden – a place to quiet down, to observe, and to cultivate reciprocity between ourselves and the land. Come join us in the visioning and stewardship of Temperance Sanctuary: as a time capsule of Indigenous history and stewardship, native food/micro forest to bring back native biodiversity, and an ecological classroom to foster and practice our stewardship. If you’re interested in any of these topics, we welcome you to join us in its design and execution!

events.title: Queering Nature
events.description:
Come enjoy a playful evening of celebrating the wonder and beauty of queerness in nature.

Inspired byDr. Patricia Ononiwu Kaishian’s book “Forest Euphoria: The Abounding Queerness of Nature”.

Fungi, we learn, commonly have more than two biological sexes—and some as many as twenty-three thousand. Some intersex slugs mutually fire calcium carbonate “love darts” at each other during courtship. Glass eels are sexually undetermined until their last year of life, which stumped scientists once dubbed “the eel question.” Nature, Kaishian shows us, is filled with the unusual, the overlooked, and the marginalized—and they have lessons for us all.

The evening will be gently facilitated through a reading, interactive game, and discussion. No need to have read the book and no prior knowledge expected or required.

hosted by Maggie and Savannah

events.title: Paint Your Grief
events.description:
Are you grieving the loss of a loved one? a pet? a break up? changes to your body? or a dream that is no longer serving you? Come paint through your grief with local portrait artist Ellie.

In this workshop, she’ll provide a demo on a tried-and-true way to paint a moving portrait. This can be a self-portrait conveying how you’ve changed, a portrait of your person, or a portrait of the friends carrying you through. Interwoven throughout, she will provide reflection questions and opportunities for you to share about your grief.*

No painting or drawing experience required. Acrylic paint and primed, unstretched canvas or cardboard to paint on will be provided.

Please come prepared with the following:

• Take time to journal. What grief is heavy on your heart now? If it is too soon to make art about it, is there another grief journey you are finally able to engage with?
• Bring reference photos related to your grief. They can be of yourself, your person, your friends, animal, etc. It’s helpful if they are high quality and if you’re a beginner, mouth closed is easiest.
• Any supplies you want. Especially if you want to work in another type of artistic medium.

*Ellie is bringing her perspective as an artist and fellow human experiencing loss and is not a licensed therapist.

This practice uses meditation, visualizations, affirmations, and particular hand placements in order to flow healing golden light through our entire being.

The attunement will be facilitated by Reverend Magdalen Rose Cammaroto, an ordained minister of the House of the Golden Light and current Vice President of the organization. This attunement is offered by donation – all proceeds directly fund the healing programs of the House of the Golden Light on Big Island, Hawai'i. These creative experiments include making photo prints (phytograms and cyanotypes) with the Mt. Plantry Film Group and weaving with grasses. Please wear close-toed shoes and long pants if you wish to participate in thinning overgrowth.

The Temperance Sanctuary is a new extension of the Temperance Alley Garden – a place to quiet down, to observe, and to cultivate reciprocity between ourselves and the land. Come join us in the visioning and stewardship of Temperance Sanctuary: as a time capsule of Indigenous history and stewardship, native food/micro forest to bring back native biodiversity, and an ecological classroom to foster and practice our stewardship. If you’re interested in any of these topics, we welcome you to join us in its design and execution!

Jenna is a poetic singer-songwriter and powerhouse vocalist who is known for her intimate acoustic performances. Based in her home state of Virginia, she’s influenced by the textures and harmonic complexity of the jazz, R&B and folk music she grew up with, and she draws inspiration from artists like Ryan Beatty, Adrianne Lenker, and Eloise. Treating her writing as an opportunity to connect our expansive human experience to the world around us, Jenna delivers introspective lyrics with soulful vocals, all carried by contemplative harmonies on her acoustic guitar, telling the hard truths that come with being human and writing love letters to the tiny beauties of everyday life.

Commanding a three-octave range and a sentimental nature, Veronique is a DC-based singer-songwriter and a lover of reproductive justice. SIRAN is a dark pop-rock project born out of Prince Georges County Maryland from brother-sister duo Tiara and Greg Byrd. Musicians by trade, they combine their influences being raised by a jazz musician and listening to grunge and indie rock from the 90s and 00s. We want people to let their hearts hang low as layered guitars wash over them in rapture when they hear our music. To give them the space to cry and dance at the same time, because life is f*** up and beautiful like that.

Los Locos is a musicalized poetry project that blends cumbia, rock, and jazz to explore themes of immigration, identity, and latinidad. Using a wide range of Latin American rhythms, Los Locos brings poetry into spaces where it’s rarely found - from bars and street corners to music stages and cultural gatherings. Unapologetic and unfiltered, Los Locos breaks open the space between music and poetry, daring audiences to keep up.

events.title: Improv at the Garden
events.description:
Improvisational theater is an unplanned, spontaneously and collaboratively created experience that exists only in the present moment. A moment that ends as quickly as it starts, like the flame on a match.

Improv at the Garden will be a series of Improv games and warm-ups that help us align with being present in the moment. It will culminate in a 10-minute montage where we can take what we learn in the warm-ups to create an experience that will never be made again.

Temperance Alley Garden is the perfect host; much like Improv Temperance exists in a temporary space, it may not exist forever, but that does not mean the stories it tells or the relationships it fosters are not meaningful. Both Improv and Temperance teach us to truly savor the moment, pay attention, actively listen, and most importantly, engage with each other.

events.title: Save a Tree, Plant a Forest 🌳
events.description:
Join us in our ongoing efforts to restore the ecology of the Temperance Alley Sanctuary.

This afternoon we will be, gathering non-native plants for future paper-making, transplanting native plants to give away to attendees, and planting tree and understory seedlings. The goal of the event is to increase the genetic and species diversity in the sanctuary in order to restore the ecology of the space. Learn how to rescue plant seedlings around your neighborhood, how to temporarily keep them alive in a pot, and how / where to plant them so they can thrive.

The Temperance Sanctuary is a new extension of the Temperance Alley Garden – a place to quiet down, to observe, and to cultivate reciprocity between ourselves and the land. Come join us in the visioning and stewardship of Temperance Sanctuary: as a time capsule of Indigenous history and stewardship, native food/micro forest to bring back native biodiversity, and an ecological classroom to foster and practice our stewardship. If you’re interested in any of these topics, we welcome you to join us in its design and execution!

events.title: Community Art Visioning for DC’s Ecological Futures at Temperance Alley Sanctuary 🎨🌿
events.description:
After a long winter of snowcrete, join us in reconnecting with land in a guided community visioning through art and meditation at Temperance Alley Sanctuary. As climate change continues to impact our urban environments, this collective visioning allows us to time travel and reimagine a joyful ecological future in DC. We’ll start by walking through the existing nature and history of the land at the Sanctuary, have a time-traveling meditation session, and create art from our visions to help us create a deeper relationship with the land and guide our restoration actions for the season.

The Temperance Sanctuary is an extension of the Temperance Alley Garden – a place to quiet down, to observe, and to cultivate reciprocity between ourselves and the land. Come join us in the visioning and stewardship of Temperance Sanctuary: as a time capsule of Indigenous history and stewardship, native food/micro forest to bring back native biodiversity, and an ecological classroom to foster and practice our stewardship in community. If you’re interested in any of these topics, we welcome you to join us in its design and execution!

hosted by Amy and Chandan

events.title: Spoken Poetry Night: Come be HOME FREE by Aparna Paul
events.description:
Come join in an evening of spoken poetry with Aparna Paul, who will be performing poetry excerpts from her debut book, HOME FREE. This event is part of her national book tour and she will also be joined by a few local DMV artists!

HOME FREE is a work of weaving. Weaving personal anecdote, family lore, collective history, fast food drive-thru & heritage home cooking, the dinner table & the house party, this language’s capacity to harm & heal, snakes & more snakes, this collection refuses to hold one truth at a time. These poems and their speaker don’t belong exactly anywhere; rather, they seek home in new ways: in people, in memory, in an open invitation to find yourself everywhere.

Aparna Paul (she/her) is a writer, chemical engineer, banana bread enthusiast, & amateur crossword constructor based in Cambridge, MA. Her poetry & prose has been recognized by Reckoning, DMQ Review, & Gaining Ground, among others. She edited the anthology Reflections of The Land (Literary Cleveland, 2022) and is a co-editor of GOOD SOUP, now on hiatus. She performs regularly, hosts occasionally, and slams sometimes at the Boston Poetry Slam at the Cantab Lounge. HOME FREE (Game Over Books, 2025) is her debut full-length poetry collection.

hosted by Natalie and Amy

events.description:
Spring time means growing season in the garden and at home. April is a great time to propagate house plants and grow your indoor garden. Join us for a house plant swap to learn about caring for new plants and take home some new plant babies! Experienced home gardeners and interested first-time houseplant growers are welcome to soak up some knowledge and walk away with a clipping.

events.title: She Cried That Day: Documentary Screening
events.description:
Join us for a free screening of the documentary “She Cried That Day.”
#MMIW #MMIWG2S

On Saturday, April 28, 2015, Christine, a young Arikara, Dakota & Diné woman, received a call that her older sister, Dione, was fighting for her life in the ICU after being found bloody and unconscious in a motel room in Gallup, NM. The police had been called to the room that Dione was sharing with her boyfriend, three times that night over complaints of people fighting. Ultimately, Dione would succumb to her horrific injuries leaving the family questioning the suspicious nature of her death. An arrest was never made.

​​As Christine and her family navigate a broken system in search for justice, we are witness to the triumphs and the defeats. By examining her personal journey, the systemic racism, generational trauma, jurisdictional and structural nightmares become tangible. The personal IS political. The microcosm is the macrocosm.​

She Cried That Day shows us first-hand, how this crisis affects a family, a community, a state, and a nation while being inspired by the strength and power of these incredible women as they fight to bring their lost sisters home. MMIWG2S stands for Missing and Murdered Indigenous Women, Girls, and Two-Spirit people. It is a grassroots movement highlighting the disproportionate rates of violence, murder, and disappearance affecting Indigenous women and LGBTQ+ individuals.

»View the trailer here«

hosted by Hope and Stephen

events.title: Bringing Ecology Back: 3D Mapping to Rewild a Vacant Lot
events.description:

Using garden stakes and string, we’ll physically map out last month’s community visioning ideas on the land, such as winding paths, hammocks, and pollinator/bird patches that invite both people and wildlife to thrive.

You’ll also learn how to properly transplant native plants and relocate them, collaborate with neighbors, and help select native plants that will transform it into a sanctuary that supports an ecologically resilient DC.

About the project: The Temperance Sanctuary is an extension of the Temperance Alley Garden – a place to quiet down, to observe, and to cultivate reciprocity between ourselves and the land. Come join us in the rewilding and stewardship of Temperance Sanctuary as a rewilded sanctuary to bring back native biodiversity, a time capsule of DC’s Indigenous history, and an ecological classroom to practice community land stewardship. We welcome you to join us in its design and rewilding!

This immersive experience invites you to slow down, reconnect, and journey inward through the healing power of sound. Using Tibetan singing bowls, voice, flute, and intuitive sound, you will be gently guided into a deep meditative state. The vibrations work throughout the body to release tension, calm the nervous system, clear emotional blockages, and restore a sense of balance and harmony.

This is more than a sound bath—it is a sacred space for reflection, healing, and reconnection with your true self.

What to expect:
• A peaceful and welcoming atmosphere in nature
• Guided relaxation and meditation through sound
• Tibetan singing bowls, flute, voice, and intuitive sound healing
• Deep rest, inner stillness, and nervous system restoration
• An opportunity to reconnect with yourself on a deeper level

No previous meditation experience is necessary. Simply come as you are, bring an open heart, and allow yourself to receive.

Join Sisi Soul Shine for the Soul Shine Theater Garden season 2 opener. We will play, breathe, hear what Sisi is doing/has coming up, and gather in collective joy, inviting joy not absent of grief, heartache, tragedy but alongside and despite of. This opener will include abundant offerings:

• Embodying the Elements movement practice,
• A presentation about the first Soul Shine Theater Garden after school residency "Imagining the Elements: Learning History through Nature and Imaginative Play" at Choptank Elementary that taught about Maryland landscapes and Harriet Tubman,
• An introduction to and exploration of Playback Theater for theater and garden folks, ending with arts and crafts. Playback theater is an improvisational form of theater where a person shares a story and an ensemble plays back that story through acting/dance/song/music. A few folks from the garden community when prompted by Sisi will be asked to tell a story so that the ensemble can practice/learn. We will learn, explore, and be curious together!

Together, we’ll kick off the physical transformation of this community rewilding project called Temperance Alley Sanctuary. events.title: Offline Connections CHALLENGE WEEK: Talking to Strangers
events.description:
Talking to Strangers *CHALLENGE WEEK*

What if you stood next to your soulmate at the bus stop without knowing it? Every day we pass up dozens of opportunities to connect with the people all around us. Even if they don’t yield lasting connections, conversations with strangers are a portal to fascinating, funny, beautiful worlds. Yet in a world where everyone is increasingly sucked into the addicting and comfortable flatlands of their phones, striking up conversation has begun to feel risky, uncomfortable, and rare.

Fill your life with spontaneity and meaningful connection, by making friends and finding partners the “old fashioned way” (in three dimensions). It doesn’t have to be scary! Join this week of challenges, supported by a positive group of fellow brave people, to rediscover the art of talking to strangers. The shy, socially anxious, and awkward are especially encouraged to join and step out of your comfort zone.

At this event, we will talk about how phone culture has shifted the way we meet people, what we’re losing, and prepare for a week of practicing authentic connections! Then, we will send you into the week with a set of challenges designed to get you to look up, be present, be brave, and talk to strangers. They don’t bite!

This is an Attention Sphere event hosted by Kendall & Luca

Part 2 (where we party and celebrate your week of breaking open a new world) is on June 18th!

Which room will give my plant the sunlight it needs? What do these brown spots on the leaves mean? The doctor's in — stop by to get their prescription for keeping your plant happy and healthy.

Little Jungle Plant Company is a local plant care service run by an actual DC native gal with 12 years in the plant and garden care business. What works for your space — indoor jungle, outdoor patio, shady corners, sunny decks. Ask the doc!

Activities include a walkthrough of the Temperance Alley Garden and its evolution through community storytelling and rewilding (particularly with the Temperance Alley Sanctuary), a guided conversation on preserving memory and history, and an arts-based reflection on how you want to carry your story forward via archiving, storytelling, scrapbooking, etc. If interested, please bring photos to collage and any scrapbooking/archiving materials you may desire to use or share.

hosted by Alisha, Amy, and Kunal.

events.title: 12 hr Film Festival: TAG in to make Film in a Day
events.description:
Writer’s block? Not enough time? Daydream of being a Director? Scriptwriter? Producer? Cinematographer? Actor? Editor? Or seeking a good time?

Let’s lean into play and discover our films together! Meet your neighbors at Temperance Alley Garden (TAG) and disperse to make a short together in 12hrs.

Here is how the day will go:

💭 Sunday 7/19 at 8-10am – Meet up, form groups (if interested) and brainstorm ideas for the short films! Feel free to come with a basic premise but otherwise the full process should take place over the weekend. It's ok to just arrive with a blank slate too! We will have brainstorming ideas for types of characters, settings, and plot lines for crafting a short film. If you can't make the early meetup then no fear - let us know and we will pair you with a group!

🎥 We invite you to discover your film by spending the day around the city, writing/filming/editing and other chaotic inputs of making a film. The goal is to keep films to around 3 minutes. It does not have to follow traditional formats, we encourage play and new ideas for what a film could (a series of vertical videos, etc.) "Zero Budget" works encouraged - phones will suffice for video and iMovie/Canva can work as an editing software.

🍿 7:30pm at Temperance Alley Garden – We gather to watch our creations! Snacks, drinks and great company provided. Films must be submitted by 8pm to abide by the 12 hour rule! Prizes (see below) will also be awarded!

This doesn’t have to be an all day undertaking! You are welcome to fully engross in the filmmaking process for the whole day or simply act as a background extra for a couple minutes. We would love to have you! Invite your creative friends and artistic rivals!!

Absolutely no experience is necessary - let's just enjoy playing with film together!

Grand Jury Prizes:
🏅 Most Niche DC reference
🏅 Best Temperance Alley Garden reference
🏅 Most Daring*
🏅 Most Experimental
🏅 Silliest Dance Sequence
🏅 Most whimsical

*Don’t get arrested

events.description:

A sculptor preparing to open a new show must balance her creative life with the daily dramas of family and friends in Kelly Reichardt's vibrant and captivatingly funny portrait of art and craft.

Filament is a new screening initiative building an audience for independent and art films in Washington DC.

Living Room is a neighborhood space in Mount Pleasant to drop in, spend time, and make art. We offer drop-in hours, workshops, and community events. Our goal is simple: make creativity part of everyday life. At Living Room: making is accessible, connection is natural, and art becomes part of how we gather.

Arrive at 7:30pm to mingle and find a seat on the lawn. The screening will begin at dusk…

Thanks to A24 for making the screening possible!

events.title: Introduction to Acting: From Text to Performance
events.description:
No previous acting experience required!

This introductory workshop offers a practical exploration of the actor’s craft through voice, movement, improvisation, and scene work. We begin with a physical and vocal warm-up inspired by training methods from theatrical traditions around the world, preparing participants to work with focus, presence, and ensemble awareness.

From there, participants will be introduced to the fundamentals of text analysis through a concise handout and guided discussion. A series of improvised scenes will explore dramatic conflict by focusing on characters with opposing needs, before transitioning to “contentless scenes”-short dialogues whose words carry no inherent meaning. Using the principles of text analysis, participants will discover how objectives, relationships, and circumstances transform simple language into compelling dramatic action, culminating in a final round of scene presentations.

Co-hosted by Nick & Zoe

Nick is a director of contemporary performance specializing in devised theatre and reimaginings of classic texts. He apprenticed under Lee Breuer, a key figure in American experimental theatre, and earned an MFA in Directing from UC San Diego, where he also taught undergraduate acting courses. His work has been presented in Los Angeles, New York, and Montana. He is currently developing theatre productions in Milan with Civil Words APS.

events.title: Scripting Worlds: Feel & Flow Writing Workshop
events.description:
Scripting Worlds is a flow-paced creative gathering for anyone who needs a reason to slow down and think (or feel) — without an agenda, a deadline, or a blank page that stares back.

We'll start with a calming body-based practice to help you move from "go-mode" into something quieter (think: less tension, more breathing room). From there, it's open writing and illustration time — completely unstructured, prompted only by a single word, phrase or question to get you started. You can write toward the life you want. Draft the first chapter of something. Process a hard week. Dream up something bold, half-formed, or completely new.

The point isn't productivity, it's permission without a pressing need to finish — just start. You don't have to be a writer or an artist to attend. Just show up & explore more of your imaginative side :)

What to Bring:

–Yourself
–Something to drink
–Something comfortable to sit on (i.e. mat, blanket, chair, pillow)

What to Expect:

–Reflection
–Creativity
–Good company

Come as you are. Leave with a little more clarity, a little more breathing room, and maybe something that surprises you. 🌱

hosted by Nayo, Kunal, & Amy

Join us in the Temperance Alley Sanctuary rewilding project to explore the flavors of our native plants. We'll be tasting a variety of teas and dishes prepared with foraged ingredients as we discuss the history and tradition of plants as food and medicine. We also welcome you to bring a foraged tea or dish.

The Temperance Alley Sanctuary is a community rewilding project of the Temperance Alley Garden – a place to quiet down, to observe, and to cultivate reciprocity between ourselves and the land. We welcome you to join in rewilding this urban lot to bring back native biodiversity, a time capsule of DC’s Indigenous history, and an ecological classroom to practice community land stewardship.

Bring a reusable cup for teas (hot and iced) and any foraged dishes you'd like to share.
